task: Finalize this Cedarbench recovery reference for support operators and notebook owners.
source_facts: Cedarbench is a synthetic managed-notebook service. All policy facts and examples below are authoritative within this case. Recovery eligibility is 7 days for draft notebooks, 30 days for published notebooks, and 14 days for attached media. A day is exactly 24 hours, measured in UTC from the recorded removal timestamp. Item class is the class at removal, not a class requested afterward. Only the item's owner can submit a qualifying request; workspace membership and a forwarded message from an owner are insufficient. A complete request includes item identifier, removal timestamp, and destination workspace and is submitted through the owner's account. Eligibility is evaluated at receipt of the complete request, not at the later time an operator opens it. A request received exactly at the cutoff qualifies. An incomplete request does not reserve eligibility; the complete version must arrive within the window. Processing delay after qualifying receipt does not make a request ineligible. Every recovery creates a new private copy in the specified destination workspace, leaves the removed item removed, and does not replace an existing notebook. The destination must be one the owner can access. Publication and sharing settings are not inherited. The owner can inspect the new copy directly as soon as recovery completes. Its search entry appears within 2 hours of recovery completion; the search clock begins at completion, not request receipt. Notebook and media eligibility are evaluated independently, even when a single request lists both. A recoverable notebook can lack ineligible media, and eligible media can be recovered without an eligible parent notebook. Support must not describe the notebook's longer window as extending its media window. At an age of 10 days, a draft notebook is ineligible and its attached media is eligible. At 20 days, a published notebook is eligible and its attached media is ineligible. A draft removed at 09:00 UTC on April 3, 2033 has its cutoff at 09:00 UTC on April 10, 2033. Complete receipt at that instant qualifies; receipt one second later does not. A request for that item first submitted without a destination at 08:50 on April 10 and completed at 09:05 is late. An eligible published notebook request received on day 29 remains eligible if an operator processes it on day 31. A recovery completed at 16:20 UTC has its search deadline at 18:20 UTC. A recovery completed at 23:30 UTC on April 10 has its search deadline at 01:30 UTC on April 11; midnight neither resets nor shortens the two-hour interval. Independent reader journeys: support operators use only the Quick lookup table, embedded in a compact console panel without surrounding prose. Owners arrive directly at Owner walkthrough from a help link; that view omits the operator table. Clock and eligibility examples are a linked explanation owners can open when interpreting a boundary case. The table and owner walkthrough must each carry the three windows, requester restriction, recovery destination behavior, and search delay. Their duplication serves separate interfaces.
draft:
# Cedarbench recovery reference

This reference supports two views of the recovery policy. The operator console displays the quick lookup table, while the owner help view opens at the walkthrough. Clock examples explain how receipt time and item class affect an individual request. Use the recorded removal event when checking eligibility.

## Quick lookup table

| Policy field | Value | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft notebook window | 7 days | Use the notebook's class at removal. |
| Published notebook window | 30 days | A later processing date does not change qualifying receipt. |
| Attached media window | 14 days | Evaluate media independently of its notebook. |
| Eligible requester | Item owner only | Workspace membership does not establish ownership. |
| Recovery result | New private copy in the specified destination workspace, which the owner must be able to access | The removed item remains removed. |
| Search availability | Within 2 hours of recovery completion | Direct inspection is available at completion. |

## Owner walkthrough

### Identify the item you need

A draft notebook can be recovered for 7 days after removal. A published notebook can be recovered for 30 days after removal. Use the notebook's class when it was removed: selecting a different intended use for the recovered material does not reclassify the removed item. This distinction matters when several notebooks with similar names had different publication states.

Attached media has a 14-day recovery window. Its eligibility is separate from the notebook that referenced it. You can list a notebook and its media in one request, but putting them together does not give every listed item the same deadline. Check which item you are asking to recover rather than assuming the parent notebook's status covers everything attached to it.

### Submit through the owner's account

Only the item owner can submit a qualifying recovery request. Being a member of the workspace does not establish that you own the removed item. A forwarded message from the owner also does not substitute for a request submitted through that owner's account. This restriction identifies whose request can qualify; it does not change the length of any item window.

Include the item identifier, its removal timestamp, and the destination workspace. Choose a destination workspace that you can access. These details make the request complete and identify both the removed material and where its recovered copy should go. If a required detail is missing, the receipt of that incomplete form does not hold a place inside the eligibility window.

### Inspect the recovered result

Recovery creates a new private copy in the specified destination workspace. The removed item remains removed, and an existing notebook is not replaced. Treat the result as a separate copy to inspect, rather than as the old item silently returning to its previous public location. Publication and sharing settings are not inherited, so the recovered result does not resume the removed item's visibility.

You can inspect the copy directly as soon as recovery completes. Its search entry appears within 2 hours of recovery completion. That interval starts when the copy is ready, not when you submitted the request. An absent search result during that interval is therefore different from an absent recovered copy: direct inspection and search availability are two distinct milestones.

## Clock and eligibility examples

### Establish the receipt boundary

A policy day is exactly 24 hours. Calculate the cutoff in UTC from the recorded removal timestamp, then compare it with the time the complete request was received. The operator's later opening of the request is not the eligibility event. A processing queue does not shorten a window that the owner met at receipt.

For a draft removed at 09:00 UTC on April 3, 2033, the cutoff is 09:00 UTC on April 10, 2033. A complete request received exactly at that cutoff qualifies. A complete request received one second later does not. The boundary includes the cutoff instant; it is not rounded to the end of the calendar date shown in the removal record.

An incomplete request does not reserve eligibility. Suppose the owner first submits that draft's request at 08:50 on April 10 but omits the destination workspace. If the complete version arrives at 09:05, it is late. The earlier partial submission cannot supply the qualifying receipt time for information that arrived after the cutoff.

### Evaluate related items separately

At an age of 10 days, a draft notebook is outside its window, while its attached media remains eligible. Recovering the eligible media does not make the notebook eligible again. The request can therefore produce a useful media copy without producing a recovered parent notebook. That result follows the two item classes rather than the fact that they once appeared together.

At an age of 20 days, a published notebook remains eligible, while its attached media is outside its window. The recovered notebook can consequently lack that media. Do not interpret the notebook's longer retention as an extension for the attachment. Listing both items on the same request leaves their separate eligibility calculations intact.

### Separate eligibility from completion

A complete, otherwise qualifying published-notebook request received on day 29 remains eligible if an operator processes it on day 31. Receipt established eligibility while the notebook was inside its window. Processing time determines when the new copy becomes available, but it does not replace receipt time in the window calculation.

If that recovery completes at 16:20 UTC, its search deadline is 18:20 UTC. The owner can inspect the private copy directly at completion instead of waiting for search. When discussing progress, identify whether the question concerns qualifying receipt, completed recovery, or search indexing. Those timestamps describe different events and answer different questions about the same request.

For a recovery completed at 23:30 UTC on April 10, search must be available by 01:30 UTC on April 11. Crossing midnight does not restart the interval or shorten it to the remaining half hour of April 10. Compare full timestamps, including dates, when a completion occurs near the end of a UTC day.
